candidate.title: CITE-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina CITE-Seq row: antibody-DNA labeling of cell-surface epitopes, co-capture with polyadenylated transcripts on cell-barcoded beads in droplets, joint production of barcode-linked DNA products, and size separation into transcript and antibody-tag fractions with coupled sequence readout. The primary paper resolves this as its depicted Drop-seq-based CITE-seq implementation; Drop-seq is the embedded compartment/capture component, not an additional target method. The partial DroNc-seq row above, ECCITE-Seq row below, and right chemical/QR-code area are neighboring context without connecting arrows into CITE-Seq. No unshown adaptation, alternative bead-recovery ADT route, sample hashing, CRISPR readout, 10x-specific implementation, or experiment-specific settings are extracted.

states.label: Intact single-cell suspension
features: Cells provide two biological targets: polyadenylated cellular transcripts and accessible cell-surface protein epitopes.
The left single-cell icon introduces both targets; it is not a material split into separate RNA and protein preparations.

evidence.locator: CITE-Seq row, left: Single cell, PolyA RNA, Surface protein; Cells + Antibody-oligo complex; binding arrow

states.label: Antibody-DNA oligonucleotide conjugates
features: Antibodies carry antibody-identifying barcode oligonucleotides, rather than a unique cell barcode.
The inset depicts an S-S linker and a terminal AA(A)n tract.
Primary text identifies the tag as DNA with a 3′ polyA tail and attachment through its 5′ end; its sequence also supports specific amplification.
The primary implementation uses streptavidin-biotin attachment with a disulfide linker that permits release under reducing conditions; no separate reduction operation is drawn.

evidence.locator: CITE-Seq row, antibody-oligo inset: Antibody, S-S linker, Antibody barcode, AA(A)n

evidence.quote: We adopted a commonly used streptavidin-biotin interaction to link the 5’ end of oligos to antibodies, and included a disulfide link, which allows the oligo to be released from the antibody in reducing conditions (Supplementary Fig. 1a).
Highly specific, flow cytometry tested monoclonal antibodies (see below) were conjugated to oligonucleotides containing unique antibody identifier sequences and a polyA tail.

states.label: Cells bearing surface-bound antibody-oligo conjugates
features: The antibody retains its DNA identity tag while binding a cell-surface epitope.
Cellular RNA remains intracellular at this boundary.
Antibody identity reports a targeted surface marker; binding is not a guarantee of perfect specificity.

evidence.quote: Measuring protein abundance by antibodies can be complicated by non-specific binding, resulting in higher background and/or false positive results.

states.label: Oligonucleotide-functionalized capture beads
features: Bead-attached capture oligos include oligo(dT), UMI, cell barcode, and PCR handle as identified by the legend.
The cell-identifying barcode indexes the co-encapsulated cell; the UMI and antibody identity barcode have different roles.
The polyT capture end binds the polyA tail of either mRNA or an antibody-derived DNA tag.

states.label: Bead-bound mRNAs and antibody-derived DNA tags in lysed-cell droplets
features: Cell lysis exposes cellular mRNA to the bead; polyA tails on mRNA and antibody tags anneal to bead polyT capture ends.

The drawing establishes tag hybridization to the bead but does not specify S-S cleavage timing; no detached free-tag intermediate is asserted.

states.label: Mixed cell-barcoded double-stranded products

Physical droplet compartmentalization is no longer present after emulsion breakup; sequence barcodes retain the cell association.
